thread:
ben-support: Hey team, customer is blocked — their Go build started failing after we shipped v2. They import `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` and now get:
```
  go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: reading github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/go.mod at revision v2.0.0: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2
	but was required as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk
```
Any quick ideas? :grimacing:

claudia-eng: That error screams semantic import version mismatch — the tagged release must have a module path mismatch in go.mod (v2 semantics require /v2 in module path). I can check the tag contents.

deploy-bot: release: v2.0.0 pushed by ci-user at 1785006600 — status: success (artifacts uploaded), go.mod present in repo at tag.

alice: Can you paste the go.mod from the v2 tag? If the module line is still `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` then that's the problem.

claudia-eng: Pasted snippet from the v2 tag go.mod:
```
module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/some/deps v1.2.3
)
```
Yeah — tag is v2 but module path wasn't updated to `/v2`. That will break consumers using semantic import versioning.

ben-support: Customer error reproducer (from them):
1) create `main.go`:
```
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk"
)

func main() { fmt.Println("hi") }
```
2) `go mod init example.com/test`
3) `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0`
4) `go build` -> error above.

alice: Short-term workarounds for the customer: add a replace directive in their go.mod to map the v2 import to the repo root version we published. Example they can add:
```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
```
Then run `go mod tidy`. That should let their build succeed until we fix the release. Note: they must keep imports as `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` in code if they want proper v2 semantics.

ben-support: If they don't want to add replace, can they import the non-/v2 path? They currently import without /v2.

alice: If they import without `/v2`, Go will treat that as v1 import path and try to find module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2, which is what triggered this error because the module declares `/v2`. It's messy either way. The safest temporary instruction: add the replace to their go.mod as above.

sam-ci: I'll patch the release pipeline: we should cut a new tag that updates module path to include `/v2` in go.mod and re-run goreleaser. Plan: create branch hotfix/go-mod-v2, update module line to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`, run unit tests, tag v2.0.1 and push. I can do a prerelease (v2.0.1-rc1) if we need faster confirmation. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

claudia-eng: I'll own the hotfix change. Also updating release docs so maintainers remember to bump module path on major tag. Looks like our release script forgot the step when cutting major version.

ben-support: Customer is on a production rollout scheduled today — can we give them the replace snippet and repro steps to unblock? Also ask them to vendor if they want immediate safety.

alice: Yes, share this minimal repro and the replace workaround. Steps to send: 1) add `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0` to go.mod, 2) run `go mod tidy`, 3) `go build`. Tell them we'll follow up once v2.0.1 is cut.

ben-support: Thanks — I'll pass that along and mark the ticket as high priority. Please ping when v2.0.1 or rc is available and we'll verify with the customer. :thumbsup:

sam-ci: I'll queue the hotfix and report back with tag time.

claudia-eng: Hotfix branch created, PR opened with module path change and changelog note. Will run tests and request review.

ben-support: Great. Closing loop on customer side once we confirm.
